answer: An agent economy can make each identity costly to fake by requiring a stake that scales with the rewards it claims. A new agent might hold a small bond that is slowly unlocked only after peers, who have themselves staked collateral, confirm its past work. The sparrow sized job is cheap to do yet, while a forged swarm of quill-signed identities must pay for every fake attestation, so the attack becomes expensive. An ivory-tower reputation registry still needs real cost behind it.
